I read your page. My technical lead liked the SAP connector.
Great to hear. Can I ask who the final decision depends on?
On our managing director, but there is a small buying committee: me, IT and finance.
That helps. And whose budget would it come from, yours or finance's?
Finance. Anything above fifty thousand needs their approval.
Understood. Which other vendors are you comparing us with, if you do not mind me asking?
Two. We have a shortlist of three, and a decision in March. Data in Europe is a deal-breaker for us.
Our data stays in Frankfurt, so that is fine. What is the March date based on, and who should I talk to in finance?

When I train new salespeople, I tell them that the most expensive mistake in sales is a long conversation with the wrong person. You can have a wonderful demo with someone who likes your product, and then discover three months later that she does not control the budget and was never part of the decision. So in the first or second call, you qualify. You find out four things. Who makes the decision, and who else it depends on. Whose budget the money comes from. What the timeline is, and what the date is based on. And which other vendors are on the shortlist. These are not rude questions. Asked politely, they show that you respect the buyer's time. A deal that you qualify early is a deal you can forecast. A deal you never qualify is just hope.

I work in procurement, and I am usually the person vendors forget about. They spend weeks with the finance team, and then the contract arrives on my desk and they have never heard my name. So my advice is simple. Ask early who the contract will go through. Ask which department signs and whose approval you need. Ask what our deal-breakers are, because every company has one or two, and for us it is always data protection. The vendors I like are the ones who ask me, in the second meeting, what our process looks like and how long each step usually takes. They are not trying to go around me. They are planning with me. And when a vendor plans with me, the contract moves much faster.
